summary: याचिका संख्या/Petition No 233/AT/2026 कोरम/ Coram: श्री जिश्नु बरुआ, अध्यक्ष / Shri Jishnu Barua, Chairperson श्री रमेश बाबू व., सदस्य / Shri Ramesh Babu V., Member श्री हरीश ददु ानी, सदस्य / Shri Harish Dudani, Member श्री रविन्द्र स हिं ढिल्लो, सदस्य / Shri Ravinder Singh Dhillon, Member आदेश ददन िंक/ Date of Order 26th of October, 2026 IN THE MATTER OF: Petition under Section 63 of the Electricity Act, 2003 for Adoption of Tariff discovered through Competitive Bidding Process for Supply of 1200 MW Firm and Dispatchable Power (Round the- Clock (RTC)) from ISTS- Connected Renewable Energy (RE) Power Projects in India under Tariff-based Competitive Bidding. And In the matter of: SJVN Limited 6th Floor, Tower-1, Office Block, NBCC Complex, East Kidwai Nagar, New Delhi -110023 ... Petitioner Versus M/s ReNew Solar Power Private Limited ReNew.Hub, Commercial Block-I, Zone-6, Golf Course Road, DLF City Phase-V, Gurugram-122009 Order in Petition No. 233/AT/2026 Page 1 4. Clarification No. 1 vide which the Pre-Bid 18.10.2024 queries of the bidder were addressed 5. Amendment No. 1 to the RfS amending the 18.10.2024 Terms and Conditions of the RfS 6. Corrigendum No. 2 to extend the bid 28.10.2024 submission date till 14.11.2024 7. Corrigendum No. 3 to extend the bid 11.11.2024 submission date till 29.11.2024 8. Last date and time of online bid submission 29.11.2024 by 14:00 hours 9. Date and time of opening of Technical bids 03.12.2024 by 15:00 hours 10. Opening of Financial bids 27.02.2025 11. Date of e-reverse auction 27.02.2025 12. Issuance of the LOAs to the successful 01.05.2025 bidders (i) Originally, the last date of submission of the bid was 08.10.2024. However, the last date for receipt of bids was extended up to 29.11.2024 from time to time through corrigenda to the RfS. (j) Accordingly, the technical bids were opened on 03.12.2024. Responses to the RfS were received from the following five bidders for a cumulative capacity of 560 MW against the tendered capacity of 1200 MW. S. Name of Bidders Contracted No. Capacity Quoted (MW) M/s Tata Power Renewable Energy Limited 200 1. M/s Dineshchandra R Agrawal Infracon Pvt. Limited 100 2. M/s EG Energy Development Private Limited 60 3. M/s ReNew Solar Power Private Limited 100 4. M/s Serentica Renewables India Private Limited 100 5. (k) The technical bids submitted by the bidders were evaluated by the Tender Committee as per the provisions of the RfS, and the technical bids of all five bidders were found technically responsive and met the required eligibility criteria for the capacities quoted by them. The cumulative capacity quoted by the technically shortlisted bidders under the RfS was 560 MW against the total Order in Petition No. 233/AT/2026 Page 7 Hearing dated 30.07.2026 10. The Petitioner updated that the Himachal Pradesh State Electricity Board Limited (HPSEB) has also filed a Petition before the State Commission under Section 86(1)(b) of the Electricity Act, 2003 seeking approval for procurement of the entire contracted quantum of power. It was further submitted that, although its consent letter dated 11.2.2026 has been placed on record, the Power Sale Agreement (PSA) with HPSEB has not yet been executed. After hearing the counsel for the Petitioner, the matter was reserved for orders. Analysis and Decision: 11. The Commission has considered the submissions of the party and now proceeds to consider the prayer of the Petitioner as regards the adoption of tariff under Section 63 of the Act for supply of 1200 MW firm and dispatchable power (Round the- Clock (RTC)) from ISTS- connected Renewable Energy (RE) Power Projects in India under Tariff-based Competitive Bidding, selected through competitive bidding process as per the Guidelines for Tariff Based Competitive Bidding Process for Procurement of Firm and Despatchable Power from Grid Connected Renewable Energy Power Projects with Energy Storage Systems dated 9.6.2023 issued by the Ministry of Power, Govt. of India under Section 63 which provides as under: “Section 63. Determination of tariff by bidding process: Notwithstanding anything contained in Section 62, the Appropriate Commission shall adopt the tariff if such tariff has been determined through transparent process of bidding in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Central Government.” 12. Thus, in terms of Section 63 of the Act, the Commission is required to adopt the tariff on being satisfied that the transparent process of bidding in accordance with the Guidelines issued by the Central Government has been followed in determining such tariff. 13. The Ministry of Power, Government of India, has notified the Guidelines under Section 63 of the Act vide Resolution No. 23/03/2023-R&R on 09.06.2023 for the Order in Petition No. 233/AT/2026 Page 12
